surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Bouchard has a goal and two assists as the Oilers beat the Rangers
paras: Matt Tomkins was back in an NHL net for the first time since Apr 17, 2024, and got the win. Connor McDavid got the scoring started for the Oilers just 50 seconds into the game, and Colton Dach extended the lead to 2-0 early in the first. Evan Bouchard stretched the lead to 3-0 on the power play midway through the second. Pavel Dorofeyev got the Rangers on the board three and a half minutes later, and Dach struck again into the empty net with 40 seconds left. Bouchard finished with a goal and two assists.
Don’t let the score fool you: the chances were a lot closer than that. Dylan Garand stopped 21 of 24 for the Rangers.

The Rangers killed off a two-man advantage that lasted a minute and a half midway through the third. The Oilers moved to 11-2-2, still first in the Pacific, while the Rangers dropped to 7-7-1, fifth in the Metropolitan.

items.text: Connor McDavid passed Glenn Anderson for fourth on the Oilers’ all-time goals list, with 418.
Mika Zibanejad passed Walt Tkaczuk for sixth on the Rangers’ all-time scoring list, with 679 points.
Connor McDavid has a point in all 15 games this season.
Three straight wins for the Oilers.
